title: Graceful interrupt, backpressure and resumable reads for Go SDK streaming
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Goal: Implement a Go SDK streaming reader pattern that cleanly propagates context cancellations and deadlines into network retry/backoff, exposes a backpressure-aware consumption API, and supports lightweight resumability for interrupted connections. This ticket focuses on the recommended ergonomics and an example reference implementation for client code (Read loop + controlled buffer) rather than changing server protocol.

Background: Current examples either block forever on slow consumers or aggressively drop partial results when the caller's context times out. Teams using the SDK embed it in HTTP handlers and workers; improper handling causes goroutine leaks, hidden retries after deadline, and surprising duplicate events. We need an approach that: 1) makes it easy to wire cancellations to network resources, 2) avoids unbounded buffering by default, 3) provides a composable resume token API for best-effort reconnects, and 4) documents recommended retry semantics for idempotent vs non-idempotent streams.
acceptance_criteria: SDK exposes a StreamReader type with a non-blocking Next(ctx) and Blocking NextBlocking(ctx, timeout) API documented for common patterns
Context cancellations and deadlines cancel in-flight reads immediately and do not produce additional retries after ctx.Done unless caller requests retry
Default buffer size is bounded and documented; SDK allows configuring buffer/backpressure strategy (drop-old, block-producer, backpressure-channels)
A minimal resume token (opaque string) is surfaced when server supports resumption; example demonstrates reconnect and resume without duplicating already-consumed items
Unit tests cover cancellation races, slow consumer backpressure, and graceful shutdown with partial aggregation preserved
Integration PR with example in examples/streaming/resumable/main.go and a runnable README showing patterns for HTTP handlers and background workers
implementation_notes: Introduce StreamReader interface: Close() error, Next(ctx) (Event, error), ResumeToken() string, Stats() string
Next(ctx) should return immediately with ctx.Err() if ctx already cancelled; network reads should select on ctx.Done() to abort outstanding net.Conn reads
Use internal bounded ring buffer (default 64 events) and a producer goroutine that fills buffer from network parser; consumers call Next which drains the buffer

Provide two consumption patterns in examples: 1) HTTP handler which uses Next with per-request ctx and aggregates partial payloads with short timeouts; 2) long-running worker that sets a long lived ctx and handles backpressure by applying configurable rate-limiter

Retry/backoff policy: do not implicitly retry indefinitely after context deadline. If resume token present, attempt N (default 3) reconnects before surface error to caller. Caller can opt-in to automatic retries via StreamOptions.AutoResume = true
Expose internal metrics (tokens_read, reconnects, buffer_drop_count) via Console instrumentation hooks (README explains mapping to Redwood Console)
Document trade-offs: blocking consumer avoids drops but may increase tail latency; drop-old keeps throughput but can lose events — choose per workload
comments: 2026-03-09 Priya Nair: Spiked several patterns last week; prototype with channel buffering + context cancel looks promising. Sharing RFC link.

2026-03-10 Carlos Mendes: Implemented initial StreamReader and NextBlocking. Observed goroutine leakage when client cancelled during net.Read — need to ensure net.Conn is closed from goroutine that owns it.
2026-03-11 Ava Chen (PM): Prioritize safety for HTTP handlers (no leaks) and clear examples. If resume token can't be provided by server, SDK should surface 'resume_not_supported' error code.
2026-03-12 Carlos Mendes: Added configurable AutoResume and limit of 3 attempts; tests for race between context cancel and reconnect are flaky — increasing synchronization in tests fixed flakiness.
2026-03-13 Security review: noted that resume tokens must be treated as sensitive; recommend optional masking and short TTLs in docs. Marked security_review_required=true on ticket.
